# USD Cognitive Substrate: Cleanup Pass Blueprint

## Claude Code MoE Agent Teams — Implementation Spec

> **Target repo:** `usd-cognitive-substrate` (and `_injection` fork)
> **Scope:** Codebase hardening pass addressing external review + additional findings
> **Execution model:** 6 Claude Code agent teams, sequential with dependency gates

---

## Reconstructed Codebase Map

```
usd-cognitive-substrate/
├── cognitive_substrate/
│   ├── converter.py                    # USDAParser → SubstrateComposer → MarkdownRenderer + InjectionEngine
│   ├── cognitive_substrate_root.usda   # Sublayer composition stack
│   ├── core_substrate_v7.usda          # Base substrate definition
│   ├── diagnose_injection.py           # Diagnostic utility
│   └── grafts/
│       ├── graft_template.usda
│       ├── graft_deepseek_v32.usda
│       └── graft_digital_injection.usda
├── src/
│   └── lossless/                       # 7 modules, 154 tests
│       ├── __init__.py
│       ├── constants.py                # PHASES, EXPERTS, tolerances, FLOAT_TOLERANCE
│       ├── schema.py                   # SignalFingerprint, PhaseScore, CascadeResult, ExpertResult
│       ├── gain.py                     # g = 1 + s_NM * d, anchor exclusion
│       ├── pharmacokinetics.py         # Onset/offset exponential curves
│       ├── cascade.py                  # Routing cascade, _compute_phase_score, sparse routing
│       ├── pipeline.py                 # LosslessPipeline, 5-stage convert(), file I/O
│       └── integrity.py               # SHA256 hashes, fidelity, mixing matrix health
├── tests/
│   └── lossless/
│       └── unit/
│           ├── test_schema.py
│           ├── test_gain.py
│           ├── test_pharmacokinetics.py
│           ├── test_cascade.py
│           ├── test_pipeline.py
│           └── test_integrity.py
├── tools/
│   └── usda_to_claude_md.py
├── README.md
├── LOSSLESS_IMPLEMENTATION_BLUEPRINT.md
└── CONSISTENCY_REPORT.md
```

---

## Change Registry (Itemized)

### From External Review

| ID | Category | Change | Priority | Agent Team |
|----|----------|--------|----------|------------|
| R1 | Performance | Add `__slots__ = True` to all frozen dataclasses | HIGH | SCHEMA |
| R2 | Type Safety | Strict generics: `list[str]`, `dict[str, float]`, `tuple[PhaseScore, ...]` | HIGH | SCHEMA |
| R3 | Type Safety | Convert PHASES, EXPERTS to `Enum` or `Literal` types | HIGH | SCHEMA |
| R4 | Type Safety | `TypedDict` for mixing matrix outputs and structured dicts | MED | SCHEMA |
| R5 | Testing | Replace `abs(a - b) < TOL` with `math.isclose(a, b, abs_tol=TOL)` | MED | TESTING |
| R6 | Testing | Replace manual `try/except + assert False` with `pytest.raises()` | MED | TESTING |
| R7 | Performance | Evaluate `@functools.lru_cache` on pure functions | LOW | MATH |
| R8 | Tooling | Add `pyproject.toml` with Ruff config | MED | INFRA |
| R9 | Pipeline | Separate I/O from computation in `pipeline.py` | LOW | PIPELINE |
| R10 | Docs | Standardize docstrings (Google Style) | MED | DOCS |

### From Our Analysis (Additional)

| ID | Category | Change | Priority | Agent Team |
|----|----------|--------|----------|------------|
| A1 | Safety | Verify anchor exclusion is STRUCTURAL not parametric in `gain.py` | CRITICAL | MATH |
| A2 | Testing | Add property-based tests (Hypothesis) for cascade determinism | HIGH | TESTING |
| A3 | Testing | Add adversarial injection profile tests for mixing matrix | HIGH | TESTING |
| A4 | Testing | Test mixing matrix at `s_NM` values beyond defined profiles | HIGH | TESTING |
| A5 | Testing | Test `condition_number < 10` invariant under edge-case gains | HIGH | TESTING |
| A6 | Type Safety | Make `Phase` enum the key type for all phase-indexed dicts | HIGH | SCHEMA |
| A7 | Docs | Add module-level docstrings to all 7 lossless modules | MED | DOCS |
| A8 | Docs | Document the gain function's anchor exclusion mechanism explicitly | MED | DOCS |
| A9 | Pipeline | Add `__all__` exports to `__init__.py` | LOW | PIPELINE |
| A10 | Tooling | Add `py.typed` marker for PEP 561 compliance | LOW | INFRA |

---

## MoE Agent Teams

### Team 1: SCHEMA (Type Safety & Memory)
**Scope:** `constants.py`, `schema.py`, all import sites
**Depends on:** Nothing (runs first)

```
TASK LIST:
├─ [R1]  Add __slots__ = True to ALL @dataclass(frozen=True) classes
│        Files: schema.py (SignalFingerprint, PhaseScore, CascadeResult, ExpertResult)
│        Also check: gain.py, pharmacokinetics.py for any dataclasses
│        Verify: isinstance checks still work, pickle still works if used
│
├─ [R3]  Create Phase and Expert enums in constants.py
│        BEFORE:
│          PHASES = ["KNOWLEDGE", "CONSTITUTIONAL", "SAFETY", "CONSENT", ...]
│          EXPERTS = ["Validator", "Scaffolder", "Restorer", ...]
│        AFTER:
│          class Phase(str, Enum):
│              KNOWLEDGE = "KNOWLEDGE"
│              CONSTITUTIONAL = "CONSTITUTIONAL"
│              SAFETY = "SAFETY"
│              CONSENT = "CONSENT"
│              COST = "COST"
│              SIGNAL = "SIGNAL"
│              PROJECT = "PROJECT"
│              EXPERT = "EXPERT"
│              DOMAIN = "DOMAIN"
│              DEFAULT = "DEFAULT"
│
│          class Expert(str, Enum):
│              VALIDATOR = "Validator"
│              SCAFFOLDER = "Scaffolder"
│              ...
│
│          ANCHOR_PHASES: frozenset[Phase] = frozenset({
│              Phase.KNOWLEDGE, Phase.CONSTITUTIONAL,
│              Phase.SAFETY, Phase.CONSENT
│          })
│
│          MODULATED_PHASES: frozenset[Phase] = frozenset(
│              set(Phase) - ANCHOR_PHASES
│          )
│        Note: Use str mixin (class Phase(str, Enum)) so existing string
│        comparisons don't break during migration. Can tighten later.
│
├─ [R2]  Strict generic annotations across all modules
│        Sweep all files in src/lossless/:
│          list -> list[Phase], list[PhaseScore], etc.
│          dict -> dict[Phase, float], dict[str, PhaseScore], etc.
│          tuple -> tuple[PhaseScore, ...] or tuple[float, float]
│        Run mypy --strict after changes to verify
│
├─ [R4]  TypedDict for structured dict returns
│        Identify all functions returning plain dicts (especially mixing matrix)
│        Create typed alternatives:
│          class MixingMatrixResult(TypedDict):
│              matrix: list[list[float]]
│              determinant: float
│              condition_number: float
│              phases: list[Phase]
│
│          class IntegrityBlock(TypedDict):
│              clean_hash: str
│              anchor_hash: str
│              fidelity: float
│              mixing_det: float
│              mixing_cond: float
│
├─ [A6]  Migrate all phase-indexed dicts to use Phase enum keys
│        This is the mechanical follow-through from R3.
│        Every dict[str, X] keyed by phase name becomes dict[Phase, X]
│        Every `if phase == "KNOWLEDGE"` becomes `if phase == Phase.KNOWLEDGE`
│        Every `phases["SAFETY"]` becomes `phases[Phase.SAFETY]`
│
└─ VERIFY:
   ├─ All 154 existing tests pass (no behavioral change)
   ├─ mypy --strict reports zero errors on src/lossless/
   └─ No string phase names remain outside of Enum definitions
```

**Claude Code command:**
```
/cleanup-schema
```

**Execution instructions for Claude Code agent:**
```
Read src/lossless/constants.py and src/lossless/schema.py first.
Create Phase and Expert enums with str mixin for backward compat.
Add __slots__ = True to all frozen dataclasses.
Sweep all 7 modules for type annotation upgrades.
Create TypedDict classes for structured dict returns.
Run existing test suite after each file change to catch regressions.
Run mypy --strict src/lossless/ as final gate.
```

---

### Team 2: MATH (Gain Integrity & Memoization)
**Scope:** `gain.py`, `pharmacokinetics.py`, `integrity.py`
**Depends on:** SCHEMA (needs Phase enum)

```
TASK LIST:
├─ [A1]  CRITICAL: Verify anchor exclusion is structural
│        Read gain.py. Find the gain computation function.
│        Determine: Does it check `if phase in ANCHOR_PHASES: return 1.0`
│        BEFORE evaluating d_n? (STRUCTURAL — correct)
│        Or does it compute `1 + s * d` where d happens to be low? (PARAMETRIC — wrong)
│
│        If PARAMETRIC: refactor to structural:
│          def compute_gain(phase: Phase, s_NM: float, d_map: dict[Phase, float]) -> float:
│              if phase in ANCHOR_PHASES:
│                  return 1.0  # Structural exclusion — d_map never consulted
│              return 1.0 + s_NM * d_map[phase]
│
│        If already STRUCTURAL: document it with an explicit comment and add
│        a test that passes a d_map with anchor phases having d=999.0 and
│        verifies gain still returns exactly 1.0.
│
├─ [R7]  Evaluate lru_cache opportunities
│        Profile-worthy candidates:
│          - Gain computation: NO — inputs change per-phase, low reuse
│          - Pharmacokinetic alpha: NO — float exchange counts, near-zero cache hits
│          - Phase scoring in cascade: MAYBE — if same SignalFingerprint repeated
│            within a batch. Only add if profiling shows >10% cache hit rate.
│
│        RECOMMENDATION: Skip memoization unless profiling data justifies it.
│        Document this decision in gain.py and pharmacokinetics.py as:
│          # NOTE: lru_cache evaluated and rejected — input cardinality too high
│          # for meaningful cache hits. Re-evaluate if batch processing introduces
│          # repeated fingerprints. See CLEANUP_BLUEPRINT.md R7.
│
├─ [A8]  Document anchor exclusion mechanism
│        Add a module-level docstring to gain.py explaining:
│          - The structural vs parametric distinction
│          - Why ANCHOR_PHASES are excluded before d_map lookup
│          - The safety implication (entire injection framework depends on this)
│          - Reference to LOSSLESS_IMPLEMENTATION_BLUEPRINT.md
│
└─ VERIFY:
   ├─ Anchor exclusion is provably structural (test with d=999.0)
   ├─ All gain tests pass
   ├─ No performance regression from enum migration
   └─ Decision on lru_cache documented
```

**Claude Code command:**
```
/cleanup-math
```

---

### Team 3: TESTING (Hardening & Property-Based)
**Scope:** All files in `tests/lossless/unit/`
**Depends on:** SCHEMA + MATH (needs enums and verified gain)

```
TASK LIST:
├─ [R5]  Replace manual float comparisons with math.isclose
│        Search all test files for pattern: abs(X - Y) < FLOAT_TOLERANCE
│        Replace with: math.isclose(X, Y, abs_tol=FLOAT_TOLERANCE)

│          try:

│        from hypothesis import given, strategies as st

│            """Anchor phases return gain=1.0 at ANY injection strength."""
│            for phase in ANCHOR_PHASES:

│

│        def test_gain_modulated_monotonic(s_NM):

"""Shared constants for the Lossless Signal Architecture.

This file is THE source of truth for all magic numbers.
Every other module imports from here. No module defines its own constants.
"""

from enum import Enum


class Phase(str, Enum):
    """Cascade phase identifier.

    Inherits from str so that Phase.KNOWLEDGE == "KNOWLEDGE" is True,
    maintaining backward compatibility with string-keyed dicts.
    """

    KNOWLEDGE = "KNOWLEDGE"
    CONSTITUTIONAL = "CONSTITUTIONAL"
    SAFETY = "SAFETY"
    CONSENT = "CONSENT"
    COST = "COST"
    SIGNAL = "SIGNAL"
    PROJECT = "PROJECT"
    EXPERT = "EXPERT"
    DOMAIN = "DOMAIN"
    DEFAULT = "DEFAULT"


class Expert(str, Enum):
    """Expert identifier in the MoE system.

    Inherits from str so that Expert.VALIDATOR == "Validator" is True.
    """

    VALIDATOR = "Validator"
    SCAFFOLDER = "Scaffolder"
    RESTORER = "Restorer"
    REFOCUSER = "Refocuser"
    CELEBRATOR = "Celebrator"
    SOCRATIC = "Socratic"
    DIRECT = "Direct"


# Phase definitions - canonical ordering for all output
PHASES: list[Phase] = list(Phase)

# Anchor phases - NEVER modulated under any injection profile
ANCHOR_PHASES: frozenset[Phase] = frozenset({
    Phase.CONSTITUTIONAL, Phase.SAFETY, Phase.CONSENT, Phase.KNOWLEDGE,
})

# Modulated phases - injection applies here
MODULATED_PHASES: frozenset[Phase] = frozenset(
    p for p in Phase if p not in ANCHOR_PHASES
)

# Receptor density map (d_n values from DMF model, topology-weighted)

"""Phase definitions with anchor/modulated designation.

Each cascade phase is classified as either ANCHOR (immutable under injection)
or MODULATED (gain-modulated by injection profiles).
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from src.lossless.constants import (
    ANCHOR_PHASES,
    D_MAP,
    PHASES,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PhaseSpec:
    """A single cascade phase with its properties."""

    name: str
    index: int
    is_anchor: bool
    receptor_density: float

    @property
    def is_modulated(self) -> bool:
        return not self.is_anchor


def build_phase_registry() -> dict:
    """Build the canonical phase registry from constants.

    Returns a dict mapping phase name to Phase object.
    Order is deterministic (follows PHASES list from constants).
    """
    registry = {}
    for i, name in enumerate(PHASES):
        registry[name] = PhaseSpec(
            name=name,
            index=i,
            is_anchor=(name in ANCHOR_PHASES),
            receptor_density=D_MAP[name],
        )
    return registry


def get_ordered_phases() -> list:
    """Return Phase objects in canonical order (PHASES from constants)."""
    registry = build_phase_registry()
    return [registry[name] for name in PHASES]


def get_anchor_phases() -> list:
    """Return only anchor phases in canonical order."""
    return [p for p in get_ordered_phases() if p.is_anchor]


def get_modulated_phases() -> list:
    """Return only modulated phases in canonical order."""
    return [p for p in get_ordered_phases() if p.is_modulated]

"""Deterministic composition resolution following USD LIVRPS rules.

LOCAL > INHERITS > VARIANTSETS > REFERENCES > PAYLOADS > SPECIALIZES

In the cognitive substrate context, LIVRPS maps to:
- LOCAL: Attributes defined directly on the prim
- INHERITS: Not used (flat structure)
- VARIANTSETS: Injection profile variants (not applied in clean channel)
- REFERENCES: Cross-prim references
- PAYLOADS: Deferred loading (not used in converter)
- SPECIALIZES: Base class specialization

For the converter, the primary composition is sublayer ordering:
stronger layers (listed first) override weaker layers (listed last).
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from src.lossless.constants import PHASES


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ConflictRecord:
    """Records a composition conflict and its resolution."""

    prim_name: str
    attribute: str
    winning_value: str
    losing_value: str
    winning_layer: str
    losing_layer: str
    resolution_rule: str


def compose_livrps(
    layers: list,
) -> tuple:
    """Compose multiple prim layers into a single resolved layer.

    Args:
        layers: List of (layer_name, list[CognitivePrim]) tuples,
                ordered from WEAKEST to STRONGEST.

    Returns:
        (resolved_prims, conflict_log) where resolved_prims is a list
        of CognitivePrim in canonical PHASES order, and conflict_log
        is a list of ConflictRecord.

    The composition is DETERMINISTIC:
    - Same layers in same order always produce same result.
    - Prims are keyed by name; stronger layers overwrite weaker ones.
    - Final ordering follows PHASES from constants (not insertion order).
    """
    resolved = {}  # name -> (prim, layer_name)
    conflicts = []

    for layer_name, prims in layers:
        for prim in prims:
            if prim.name in resolved:
                old_prim, old_layer = resolved[prim.name]
                conflicts.append(ConflictRecord(
                    prim_name=prim.name,
                    attribute="markdown_content",
                    winning_value=_truncate(prim.markdown_content),
                    losing_value=_truncate(old_prim.markdown_content),
                    winning_layer=layer_name,
                    losing_layer=old_layer,
                    resolution_rule="stronger_sublayer_wins",
                ))
            resolved[prim.name] = (prim, layer_name)

    # Extract prims and sort by canonical phase order, then by priority
    prim_list = [prim for prim, _layer in resolved.values()]
    prim_list = _canonical_sort(prim_list)

    return prim_list, conflicts


def _canonical_sort(prims: list) -> list:
    """Sort prims by canonical PHASES order, then by priority, then by name.

    This sort is deterministic: same input always produces same output.
    The three-level sort key ensures no ambiguity even with equal priorities.
    """
    phase_order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(PHASES)}
    default_idx = len(PHASES)

    return sorted(
        prims,
        key=lambda p: (
            phase_order.get(p.phase, default_idx),
            p.priority,
            p.name,
        ),
    )


def apply_overrides(prims: list, overrides: list) -> list:
    """Apply override prims to resolved prims.

    Args:
        prims: Resolved prim list.
        overrides: List of (override_prim, mode) where mode is
                   "append" or "replace".

    Returns:
        New list of prims with overrides applied.
        Order is preserved (deterministic).
    """
    prim_map = {p.name: p for p in prims}

    for override, mode in overrides:
        if override.name not in prim_map:
            continue
        target = prim_map[override.name]
        if mode == "replace":
            prim_map[override.name] = target.with_content(
                override.markdown_content
            )
        elif mode == "append":
            prim_map[override.name] = target.with_content(
                target.markdown_content + override.markdown_content
            )

    # Maintain canonical sort order
    result = _canonical_sort(list(prim_map.values()))
    return result


def _truncate(text: str, max_len: int = 80) -> str:
    """Truncate text for conflict log readability."""
    if len(text) <= max_len:
        return text
    return text[:max_len] + "..."

1→"""Injection profile definitions with validation.
     2→

     4→gain(phase, profile) is the core equation: g = 1 + s * d
     5→"""
     6→
     7→import math
     8→from dataclasses import dataclass
     9→
    10→from src.lossless.constants import (
    11→    ANCHOR_PHASES,
    12→    D_MAP,
    13→    OFFSET_EXCHANGES,
    14→    ONSET_EXCHANGES,
    15→    PROFILES,
    16→)
    17→
    18→
    19→@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    20→class InjectionProfile:
    21→    """A validated injection profile.
    22→
    23→    Attributes:
    24→        name: Profile name (must be a key in PROFILES).
    25→        s_NM: Neuromodulatory signal strength.
    26→        routing: Routing mode (standard/dissolved/integrative).
    27→        cross_expert: Cross-expert bleeding coefficient.
    28→        tangent_mult: Tangent budget multiplier.
    29→    """
    30→

    32→    s_NM: float
    33→    routing: str
    34→    cross_expert: float
    35→    tangent_mult: float
    36→
    37→    def __post_init__(self):
    38→        if self.s_NM < 0.0:
    39→            raise ValueError(f"s_NM must be >= 0.0, got {self.s_NM}")
    40→        if self.s_NM > 1.0:
    41→            raise ValueError(f"s_NM must be <= 1.0, got {self.s_NM}")
    42→        if self.routing not in ("standard", "dissolved", "integrative"):
    43→            raise ValueError(f"Invalid routing mode: {self.routing}")
    44→        if self.cross_expert < 0.0 or self.cross_expert > 1.0:
    45→            raise ValueError(
    46→                f"cross_expert must be in [0, 1], got {self.cross_expert}"
    47→            )

    49→            raise ValueError(
    50→                f"tangent_mult must be >= 0, got {self.tangent_mult}"
    51→            )

    54→def load_profile(name: str) -> InjectionProfile:

    56→

    63→    Raises:

    69→            f"Unknown profile '{name}'. Valid: {valid}"

    74→        s_NM=cfg["s_NM"],
    75→        routing=cfg["routing"],
    76→        cross_expert=cfg["cross_expert"],
    77→        tangent_mult=cfg["tangent_mult"],
    78→    )

"""Injection profile definitions with validation.

Provides the InjectionProfile dataclass and the gain() function.
gain(phase, profile) is the core equation: g = 1 + s * d
"""

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass

from src.lossless.constants import (
    ANCHOR_PHASES,
    D_MAP,
    OFFSET_EXCHANGES,
    ONSET_EXCHANGES,
    PROFILES,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class InjectionProfile:
    """A validated injection profile.

    Attributes:
        name: Profile name (must be a key in PROFILES).
        s_NM: Neuromodulatory signal strength.
        routing: Routing mode (standard/dissolved/integrative).
        cross_expert: Cross-expert bleeding coefficient.
        tangent_mult: Tangent budget multiplier.
    """

    name: str
    s_NM: float
    routing: str
    cross_expert: float
    tangent_mult: float

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.s_NM < 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"s_NM must be >= 0.0, got {self.s_NM}")
        if self.s_NM > 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"s_NM must be <= 1.0, got {self.s_NM}")
        if self.routing not in ("standard", "dissolved", "integrative"):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid routing mode: {self.routing}")
        if self.cross_expert < 0.0 or self.cross_expert > 1.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cross_expert must be in [0, 1], got {self.cross_expert}"
            )
        if self.tangent_mult < 0.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"tangent_mult must be >= 0, got {self.tangent_mult}"
            )


def load_profile(name: str) -> InjectionProfile:
    """Load a named profile from constants.

    Args:
        name: Profile name (key in PROFILES dict).

    Returns:
        Validated InjectionProfile.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If profile name is unknown.
    """
    if name not in PROFILES:
        valid = sorted(PROFILES.keys())
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown profile '{name}'. Valid: {valid}"
        )
    cfg = PROFILES[name]
    return InjectionProfile(
        name=name,
        s_NM=cfg["s_NM"],
        routing=cfg["routing"],
        cross_expert=cfg["cross_expert"],
        tangent_mult=cfg["tangent_mult"],
    )


def gain(phase: str, s_NM: float) -> float:
    """Calculate gain for a phase at a given signal strength.

    g = 1 + s * d

    For anchor phases, ALWAYS returns 1.0 regardless of s_NM.
    For modulated phases, returns 1.0 + s_NM * D_MAP[phase].

    Properties:
        - gain(phase, 0.0) == 1.0 for ALL phases (identity)
        - gain(anchor_phase, any_s) == 1.0 (anchor invariance)
        - gain is continuous in s_NM (no discontinuities)
        - gain >= 1.0 always
    """
    if phase in ANCHOR_PHASES:
        return 1.0

    if phase not in D_MAP:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown phase: {phase}")

    d = D_MAP[phase]
    return 1.0 + s_NM * d


def gain_with_alpha(phase: str, s_NM: float, alpha: float) -> float:
    """Calculate alpha-weighted gain.

    Returns 1.0 + alpha * (gain(phase, s_NM) - 1.0)

    When alpha=0.0, returns 1.0 (no injection).
    When alpha=1.0, returns gain(phase, s_NM) (full injection).
    Continuous in both s_NM and alpha.
    """
    base_gain = gain(phase, s_NM)
    return 1.0 + alpha * (base_gain - 1.0)


def pharmacokinetic_alpha(
    profile_name: str,
    exchanges_since_inject: int,
    exchanges_since_off: int,
    is_active: bool,
) -> float:
    """Calculate pharmacokinetic alpha (injection strength).

    Uses exponential curves for onset and offset.

    Args:
        profile_name: Profile name.
        exchanges_since_inject: Exchanges since injection activated.
        exchanges_since_off: Exchanges since injection deactivated.
        is_active: Whether injection is currently active.

    Returns:
        Alpha in [0.0, 1.0].
    """
    if profile_name == "none":
        return 0.0

    onset = ONSET_EXCHANGES.get(profile_name, 1)
    offset = OFFSET_EXCHANGES.get(profile_name, 2)

    if is_active:
        if onset <= 0:
            return 1.0
        # Exponential onset: 1 - e^(-3 * t / onset)
        # At t=onset, alpha ~= 0.95
        t = max(0, exchanges_since_inject)
        return 1.0 - math.exp(-3.0 * t / onset)
    else:
        if offset <= 0:
            return 0.0
        # Exponential offset: e^(-3 * t / offset)
        # At t=offset, alpha ~= 0.05
        t = max(0, exchanges_since_off)
        return math.exp(-3.0 * t / offset)

Core equation: g = 1 + s_NM * d_n^rec

Anchor phases (CONSTITUTIONAL, SAFETY, CONSENT, KNOWLEDGE) are
STRUCTURALLY excluded -- the gain function returns 1.0 before
the receptor density map is consulted. This is the safety floor
of the entire injection architecture.

Properties:
    - gain(phase, 0.0) == 1.0 for ALL phases (identity)
    - gain(anchor_phase, any_s) == 1.0 (anchor invariance, STRUCTURAL)
    - gain is continuous in s_NM (no discontinuities)
    - gain >= 1.0 always

NOTE: lru_cache evaluated and rejected -- input cardinality too high
for meaningful cache hits. Each (phase, s_NM) pair is typically unique
per pipeline invocation. Re-evaluate if batch processing introduces
repeated fingerprints. See CLEANUP_BLUEPRINT.md R7.
"""

from src.lossless.constants import (
    ANCHOR_PHASES,
    D_MAP,
    PHASES,
)


def compute_gain(phase: str, s_NM: float) -> float:
    """Calculate gain for a phase at a given signal strength.

    Args:
        phase: Phase name from PHASES.
        s_NM: Neuromodulatory signal strength.

    Returns:
        Gain value >= 1.0.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If phase is unknown.
    """
    if phase in ANCHOR_PHASES:
        return 1.0

    if phase not in D_MAP:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown phase: {phase}")

    d = D_MAP[phase]
    return 1.0 + s_NM * d


def compute_gains_for_profile(s_NM: float) -> dict:
    """Compute gains for all phases at a given signal strength.

    Args:
        s_NM: Neuromodulatory signal strength.

    Returns:
        Dict mapping phase name to gain value.
        Keys are in canonical PHASES order.
    """
    result = {}
    for phase in PHASES:
        result[phase] = compute_gain(phase, s_NM)
    return result

"""Injection state management across exchanges.

Tracks current injection state including profile, exchange count,
pharmacokinetic alpha, and mixing tracker.
"""

from src.lossless.constants import PROFILES
from src.lossless.injection.gain import compute_gain
from src.lossless.injection.mixing import MixingTracker
from src.lossless.injection.pharmacokinetics import compute_alpha


class InjectionState:
    """Tracks current injection state across exchanges.

    Attributes:
        profile: Current profile name.
        exchange_count: Exchanges since injection activated.
        exchanges_since_off: Exchanges since injection deactivated.
        alpha: Current pharmacokinetic alpha [0.0, 1.0].
        active: Whether injection is currently active.
        mixing_tracker: MixingTracker for cross-expert bleeding.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.profile = "none"
        self.exchange_count = 0
        self.exchanges_since_off = 0
        self.alpha = 0.0
        self.active = False
        self.mixing_tracker = MixingTracker()

    def activate(self, profile: str) -> None:
        """Activate injection with a named profile.

        Args:
            profile: Profile name (must be in PROFILES).

        Raises:
            ValueError: If profile is unknown.
        """
        if profile not in PROFILES:
            valid = sorted(PROFILES.keys())
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown profile '{profile}'. Valid: {valid}")

        self.profile = profile
        self.exchange_count = 0
        self.exchanges_since_off = 0
        self.active = True
        self.mixing_tracker = MixingTracker()
        self._update_alpha()

        # Set up cross-expert bleeding based on profile
        cross_expert = PROFILES[profile]["cross_expert"]
        if cross_expert > 0.0:
            self._setup_bleeding(cross_expert)

    def deactivate(self) -> None:
        """Deactivate injection (begin offset ramp)."""
        self.active = False
        self.exchanges_since_off = 0
        self._update_alpha()

    def advance_exchange(self) -> None:
        """Advance one exchange and update alpha."""
        if self.active:
            self.exchange_count += 1
        else:
            self.exchanges_since_off += 1
        self._update_alpha()

    def get_gain(self, phase: str) -> float:
        """Get alpha-weighted gain for a phase.

        Returns 1.0 + alpha * (gain(phase, s_NM) - 1.0)
        """
        if not self.active and abs(self.alpha) < 1e-12:
            return 1.0

        s_NM = PROFILES[self.profile]["s_NM"]
        base_gain = compute_gain(phase, s_NM)
        return 1.0 + self.alpha * (base_gain - 1.0)

    def get_s_NM(self) -> float:
        """Get the current profile's s_NM value."""
        return PROFILES[self.profile]["s_NM"]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        """Serialize state for integrity block."""
        return {
            "active": self.active,
            "alpha": self.alpha,
            "exchange_count": self.exchange_count,
            "exchanges_since_off": self.exchanges_since_off,
            "mixing": self.mixing_tracker.to_dict(),
            "profile": self.profile,
        }

    def _update_alpha(self) -> None:
        """Recalculate alpha from pharmacokinetic model."""
        self.alpha = compute_alpha(
            self.profile,
            self.exchange_count,
            self.exchanges_since_off,
            self.active,
        )

    def _setup_bleeding(self, cross_expert: float) -> None:
        """Configure cross-expert bleeding in the mixing tracker.

        Bleeds are symmetric between adjacent modulated phases
        in canonical order.
        """
        from src.lossless.constants import MODULATED_PHASES
        mod_phases = sorted(MODULATED_PHASES)

        for i in range(len(mod_phases) - 1):
            src = mod_phases[i]
            tgt = mod_phases[i + 1]
            # Symmetric bleeding between adjacent phases
            self.mixing_tracker.record_bleed(src, tgt, cross_expert)
            self.mixing_tracker.record_bleed(tgt, src, cross_expert)

1→"""Injection delta computation.
     2→
     3→Takes a CleanConversionResult and an injection profile,
     4→produces deltas. Deltas are ADDITIVE, not replacements.
     5→final = clean + alpha * delta
     6→
     7→For anchor phases: delta is EMPTY STRING (no modification).
     8→For modulated phases: delta contains gain-annotated metadata.
     9→"""

    11→from dataclasses import dataclass
    12→
    13→from src.lossless.constants import ANCHOR_PHASES, PHASES, PROFILES
    14→from src.lossless.injection.gain import compute_gain

    17→@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    18→class InjectionDelta:
    19→    """Result of injection delta computation.
    20→
    21→    Attributes:
    22→        section_deltas: Phase-name -> markdown delta string.
    23→        gains_applied: Phase-name -> gain value used.
    24→        is_anchor: Phase-name -> whether this phase is anchor.
    25→        profile_name: Which profile was used.
    26→        s_NM: Signal strength used.
    27→    """
    28→
    29→    section_deltas: tuple  # tuple of (key, value) pairs
    30→    gains_applied: tuple   # tuple of (key, value) pairs
    31→    is_anchor: tuple       # tuple of (key, value) pairs
    32→    profile_name: str
    33→    s_NM: float
    34→
    35→    def get_deltas_dict(self) -> dict:
    36→        return dict(self.section_deltas)
    37→
    38→    def get_gains_dict(self) -> dict:
    39→        return dict(self.gains_applied)
    40→
    41→    def get_anchor_flags(self) -> dict:
    42→        return dict(self.is_anchor)
    43→
    44→    @staticmethod
    45→    def empty() -> "InjectionDelta":
    46→        """Create an empty delta (no injection)."""
    47→        deltas = tuple((p, "") for p in PHASES)
    48→        gains = tuple((p, 1.0) for p in PHASES)
    49→        anchors = tuple((p, p in ANCHOR_PHASES) for p in PHASES)
    50→        return InjectionDelta(
    51→            section_deltas=deltas,
    52→            gains_applied=gains,
    53→            is_anchor=anchors,
    54→            profile_name="none",
    55→            s_NM=0.0,
    56→        )
    57→
    58→
    59→def compute_delta(
    60→    sections: dict,
    61→    profile_name: str,
    62→) -> InjectionDelta:
    63→    """Compute injection deltas for all sections.
    64→
    65→    Args:
    66→        sections: Phase-name -> markdown mapping (from clean conversion).
    67→        profile_name: Injection profile to use.
    68→
    69→    Returns:
    70→        InjectionDelta with per-phase deltas.
    71→    """
    72→    if profile_name not in PROFILES:
    73→        raise ValueError(f"Unknown profile: {profile_name}")
    74→
    75→    s_NM = PROFILES[profile_name]["s_NM"]
    76→
    77→    section_deltas = {}
    78→    gains_applied = {}
    79→    is_anchor_map = {}
    80→
    81→    for phase in PHASES:
    82→        is_anchor = phase in ANCHOR_PHASES
    83→        is_anchor_map[phase] = is_anchor
    84→        g = compute_gain(phase, s_NM)
    85→        gains_applied[phase] = g
    86→
    87→        if is_anchor or phase not in sections:
    88→            # Anchor phases or missing phases: empty delta
    89→            section_deltas[phase] = ""
    90→        else:
    91→            # Modulated phases: compute delta content
    92→            section_deltas[phase] = _compute_section_delta(
    93→                sections[phase], g, phase, profile_name
    94→            )
    95→
    96→    return InjectionDelta(
    97→        section_deltas=tuple(sorted(section_deltas.items())),
    98→        gains_applied=tuple(sorted(gains_applied.items())),
    99→        is_anchor=tuple(sorted(is_anchor_map.items())),
   100→        profile_name=profile_name,
   101→        s_NM=s_NM,
   102→    )
   103→
   104→
   105→def _compute_section_delta(
   106→    clean_content: str, gain_value: float, phase: str, profile_name: str
   107→) -> str:
   108→    """Compute the delta for a single modulated section.
   109→
   110→    The delta is metadata that records how the section should be
   111→    annotated under injection. It does NOT modify the clean content
   112→    directly - that's the combiner's job (Agent 6).
   113→
   114→    For now, deltas are injection metadata comments that get appended.
   115→    """
   116→    if abs(gain_value - 1.0) < 1e-12:
   117→        return ""  # No modulation at gain=1.0
   118→
   119→    return (
   120→        f"\n<!-- injection: profile={profile_name} "
   121→        f"phase={phase} gain={gain_value:.6f} -->"
   122→    )

1→"""Cross-expert mixing matrix tracker.
     2→
     3→Tracks cross-expert bleeding coefficients.
     4→The mixing matrix starts as identity and records bleeds.
     5→Must remain invertible at all defined profiles.
     6→
     7→Uses pure Python (no numpy) to minimize dependencies.
     8→"""
     9→
    10→from src.lossless.constants import (
    11→    ANCHOR_PHASES,
    12→    FLOAT_TOLERANCE,
    13→    MODULATED_PHASES,
    14→)
    15→
    16→# Modulated phases in canonical sorted order
    17→_MOD_PHASES = sorted(MODULATED_PHASES)
    18→_MOD_INDEX = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(_MOD_PHASES)}
    19→_N = len(_MOD_PHASES)
    20→
    21→
    22→class MixingTracker:
    23→    """Tracks cross-expert bleeding in a mixing matrix.
    24→
    25→    The matrix is NxN where N = len(MODULATED_PHASES).
    26→    Starts as identity. Bleeds are recorded as off-diagonal entries.
    27→
    28→    Properties:
    29→        - det(matrix) > FLOAT_TOLERANCE (always invertible)
    30→        - condition_number < MAX_CONDITION_NUMBER at defined profiles
    31→        - invert(mix(signal)) == signal (within FLOAT_TOLERANCE)
    32→    """
    33→
    34→    def __init__(self):
    35→        # Initialize as identity matrix (list of lists)
    36→        self._matrix = [[0.0] * _N for _ in range(_N)]
    37→        for i in range(_N):
    38→            self._matrix[i][i] = 1.0
    39→
    40→    def record_bleed(
    41→        self, source_phase: str, target_phase: str, coefficient: float
    42→    ) -> None:
    43→        """Record a cross-expert bleed.
    44→
    45→        Args:
    46→            source_phase: Phase bleeding FROM (must be modulated).
    47→            target_phase: Phase bleeding TO (must be modulated).
    48→            coefficient: Bleed amount in [0, 1).
    49→
    50→        Raises:
    51→            ValueError: If either phase is anchor or coefficient invalid.
    52→        """
    53→        if source_phase in ANCHOR_PHASES:
    54→            raise ValueError(f"Cannot bleed from anchor phase: {source_phase}")
    55→        if target_phase in ANCHOR_PHASES:
    56→            raise ValueError(f"Cannot bleed to anchor phase: {target_phase}")
    57→        if source_phase not in _MOD_INDEX:
    58→            raise ValueError(f"Unknown modulated phase: {source_phase}")
    59→        if target_phase not in _MOD_INDEX:
    60→            raise ValueError(f"Unknown modulated phase: {target_phase}")
    61→        if coefficient < 0.0 or coefficient >= 1.0:
    62→            raise ValueError(f"Coefficient must be in [0, 1), got {coefficient}")
    63→
    64→        src_i = _MOD_INDEX[source_phase]
    65→        tgt_i = _MOD_INDEX[target_phase]
    66→        self._matrix[tgt_i][src_i] += coefficient
    67→
    68→    def determinant(self) -> float:
    69→        """Compute matrix determinant using LU decomposition."""
    70→        return _determinant(self._matrix)
    71→
    72→    def is_invertible(self) -> bool:
    73→        """Check if the mixing matrix is invertible."""
    74→        return abs(self.determinant()) > FLOAT_TOLERANCE
    75→
    76→    def condition_number(self) -> float:
    77→        """Estimate condition number (ratio of max/min singular values).
    78→
    79→        Uses a simplified estimate: ||A|| * ||A^-1|| using infinity norms.
    80→        """
    81→        norm_a = _infinity_norm(self._matrix)
    82→        try:
    83→            inv = _invert_matrix(self._matrix)
    84→        except ValueError:
    85→            return float('inf')
    86→        norm_inv = _infinity_norm(inv)
    87→        return norm_a * norm_inv
    88→
    89→    def mix(self, signal: list) -> list:
    90→        """Apply mixing matrix to a signal vector."""
    91→        if len(signal) != _N:
    92→            raise ValueError(f"Signal length must be {_N}, got {len(signal)}")
    93→        return _mat_vec_mul(self._matrix, signal)
    94→
    95→    def invert(self, mixed_signal: list) -> list:
    96→        """Recover original signal from mixed signal."""
    97→        if len(mixed_signal) != _N:
    98→            raise ValueError(
    99→                f"Signal length must be {_N}, got {len(mixed_signal)}"
   100→            )
   101→        inv = _invert_matrix(self._matrix)
   102→        return _mat_vec_mul(inv, mixed_signal)
   103→
   104→    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
   105→        """Serialize for integrity block.
   106→
   107→        Returns dict with sorted keys for determinism.
   108→        """
   109→        return {
   110→            "dimensions": _N,
   111→            "determinant": self.determinant(),
   112→            "condition_number": self.condition_number(),
   113→            "is_invertible": self.is_invertible(),
   114→            "phases": _MOD_PHASES,
   115→            "matrix": [row[:] for row in self._matrix],
   116→        }
   117→
   118→    def get_matrix_copy(self) -> list:
   119→        """Return a copy of the internal matrix."""
   120→        return [row[:] for row in self._matrix]
   121→
   122→
   123→# ── Matrix math (pure Python, no numpy) ─────────────────────────────
   124→
   125→
   126→def _mat_vec_mul(mat: list, vec: list) -> list:
   127→    """Matrix-vector multiplication."""
   128→    n = len(vec)
   129→    result = [0.0] * n
   130→    for i in range(n):
   131→        # Kahan summation for numerical stability
   132→        s = 0.0
   133→        c = 0.0
   134→        for j in range(n):
   135→            y = mat[i][j] * vec[j] - c
   136→            t = s + y
   137→            c = (t - s) - y
   138→            s = t
   139→        result[i] = s
   140→    return result
   141→
   142→
   143→def _infinity_norm(mat: list) -> float:
   144→    """Infinity norm: max absolute row sum."""
   145→    n = len(mat)
   146→    max_sum = 0.0
   147→    for i in range(n):
   148→        row_sum = sum(abs(mat[i][j]) for j in range(n))
   149→        if row_sum > max_sum:
   150→            max_sum = row_sum
   151→    return max_sum
   152→
   153→
   154→def _determinant(mat: list) -> float:
   155→    """Compute determinant via LU decomposition."""
   156→    n = len(mat)
   157→    if n == 0:
   158→        return 1.0
   159→
   160→    # Copy matrix
   161→    lu = [row[:] for row in mat]
   162→    det = 1.0
   163→
   164→    for col in range(n):
   165→        # Partial pivoting
   166→        max_val = abs(lu[col][col])
   167→        max_row = col
   168→        for row in range(col + 1, n):
   169→            if abs(lu[row][col]) > max_val:
   170→                max_val = abs(lu[row][col])
   171→                max_row = row
   172→
   173→        if max_row != col:
   174→            lu[col], lu[max_row] = lu[max_row], lu[col]
   175→            det *= -1.0
   176→
   177→        if abs(lu[col][col]) < FLOAT_TOLERANCE:
   178→            return 0.0
   179→
   180→        det *= lu[col][col]
   181→
   182→        for row in range(col + 1, n):
   183→            factor = lu[row][col] / lu[col][col]
   184→            for j in range(col + 1, n):
   185→                lu[row][j] -= factor * lu[col][j]
   186→
   187→    return det
   188→
   189→
   190→def _invert_matrix(mat: list) -> list:
   191→    """Invert matrix using Gauss-Jordan elimination."""
   192→    n = len(mat)
   193→    # Augmented matrix [A | I]
   194→    aug = [mat[i][:] + [1.0 if j == i else 0.0 for j in range(n)]
   195→           for i in range(n)]
   196→
   197→    for col in range(n):
   198→        # Partial pivoting
   199→        max_val = abs(aug[col][col])
   200→        max_row = col
   201→        for row in range(col + 1, n):
   202→            if abs(aug[row][col]) > max_val:
   203→                max_val = abs(aug[row][col])
   204→                max_row = row
   205→
   206→        if max_val < FLOAT_TOLERANCE:
   207→            raise ValueError("Matrix is singular")
   208→
   209→        if max_row != col:
   210→            aug[col], aug[max_row] = aug[max_row], aug[col]
   211→
   212→        pivot = aug[col][col]
   213→        for j in range(2 * n):
   214→            aug[col][j] /= pivot
   215→
   216→        for row in range(n):
   217→            if row == col:
   218→                continue
   219→            factor = aug[row][col]
   220→            for j in range(2 * n):
   221→                aug[row][j] -= factor * aug[col][j]
   222→
   223→    # Extract inverse
   224→    return [aug[i][n:] for i in range(n)]
   225→

1→"""10-phase cascade evaluation for routing decisions.
     2→
     3→Fixed evaluation order (PHASES from constants).
     4→Each phase returns a score and routing decision.
     5→Deterministic: same signal fingerprint -> same route, always.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→import hashlib
     9→from dataclasses import dataclass
    10→
    11→from src.lossless.constants import (
    12→    D_MAP,
    13→    HASH_ALGORITHM,
    14→    PHASES,
    15→)
    16→
    17→
    18→@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    19→class SignalFingerprint:
    20→    """A signal to be routed through the cascade.
    21→
    22→    Attributes:
    23→        emotional_valence: frustrated / calm / energized
    24→        domain_signal: vfx / web / ai_research / general
    25→        energy_level: high / medium / low / depleted
    26→        urgency: immediate / normal / exploratory
    27→    """
    28→
    29→    emotional_valence: str = "calm"
    30→    domain_signal: str = "general"
    31→    energy_level: str = "medium"
    32→    urgency: str = "normal"
    33→
    34→    def to_hash(self) -> str:
    35→        """Deterministic hash of the signal fingerprint."""
    36→        parts = [
    37→            f"ev={self.emotional_valence}",
    38→            f"ds={self.domain_signal}",
    39→            f"el={self.energy_level}",
    40→            f"ur={self.urgency}",
    41→        ]
    42→        combined = "|".join(parts)
    43→        h = hashlib.new(HASH_ALGORITHM)
    44→        h.update(combined.encode('utf-8'))
    45→        return h.hexdigest()
    46→
    47→
    48→@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    49→class PhaseScore:
    50→    """Score for a single phase in the cascade."""
    51→
    52→    phase: str
    53→    score: float
    54→    evaluated: bool  # False if skipped by sparse routing
    55→
    56→
    57→@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    58→class CascadeResult:
    59→    """Result of a full cascade evaluation.
    60→
    61→    Always contains scores for ALL 10 phases,
    62→    even if sparse routing skipped some.
    63→    """
    64→
    65→    phase_scores: tuple  # tuple of PhaseScore, always PHASE_COUNT length
    66→    selected_phases: tuple  # top phases by score
    67→    signal_hash: str
    68→    routing_mode: str  # "dense" or "sparse"
    69→
    70→    def get_scores_dict(self) -> dict:
    71→        """Return phase -> score mapping."""
    72→        return {ps.phase: ps.score for ps in self.phase_scores}
    73→
    74→
    75→def evaluate_cascade(
    76→    signal: SignalFingerprint,
    77→    active_phases: list = None,
    78→    gains: dict = None,
    79→) -> CascadeResult:
    80→    """Evaluate the 10-phase routing cascade.
    81→
    82→    Args:
    83→        signal: Signal fingerprint to route.
    84→        active_phases: If provided, only these phases are fully evaluated
    85→                      (sparse routing). All others get default score 0.
    86→        gains: Optional gain modifiers per phase (from injection).
    87→
    88→    Returns:
    89→        CascadeResult with scores for all 10 phases.
    90→    """
    91→    if gains is None:
    92→        gains = {}
    93→
    94→    signal_hash = signal.to_hash()
    95→    is_sparse = active_phases is not None
    96→
    97→    # Evaluate all phases in FIXED canonical order
    98→    phase_scores = []
    99→    for phase in PHASES:
   100→        if is_sparse and phase not in active_phases:
   101→            # Sparse: record as not evaluated
   102→            phase_scores.append(PhaseScore(
   103→                phase=phase, score=0.0, evaluated=False
   104→            ))
   105→        else:
   106→            # Dense: compute score deterministically
   107→            score = _compute_phase_score(phase, signal, signal_hash)
   108→
   109→            # Apply gain if present
   110→            g = gains.get(phase, 1.0)
   111→            score = score * g
   112→
   113→            phase_scores.append(PhaseScore(
   114→                phase=phase, score=score, evaluated=True
   115→            ))
   116→
   117→    # Select top phases by score, using phase priority as tiebreaker
   118→    scored = [(ps.score, PHASES.index(ps.phase), ps.phase)
   119→              for ps in phase_scores if ps.evaluated]
   120→    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))  # desc score, asc phase index
   121→    selected = tuple(s[2] for s in scored[:3])
   122→
   123→    routing_mode = "sparse" if is_sparse else "dense"
   124→
   125→    return CascadeResult(
   126→        phase_scores=tuple(phase_scores),
   127→        selected_phases=selected,
   128→        signal_hash=signal_hash,
   129→        routing_mode=routing_mode,
   130→    )
   131→
   132→
   133→def _compute_phase_score(
   134→    phase: str, signal: SignalFingerprint, signal_hash: str
   135→) -> float:
   136→    """Compute a deterministic score for a phase given a signal.
   137→
   138→    Uses hash-based scoring to ensure determinism.
   139→    """
   140→    # Hash phase + signal for deterministic score
   141→    h = hashlib.new(HASH_ALGORITHM)
   142→    h.update(phase.encode('utf-8'))
   143→    h.update(signal_hash.encode('utf-8'))
   144→    digest = h.hexdigest()
   145→
   146→    # Convert first 8 hex chars to a score in [0, 1]
   147→    base_score = int(digest[:8], 16) / (16**8)
   148→
   149→    # Weight by receptor density (phases with higher d get higher base scores
   150→    # for relevant signals)
   151→    d = D_MAP.get(phase, 0.5)
   152→    relevance = _signal_relevance(phase, signal)
   153→
   154→    return base_score * 0.3 + d * 0.3 + relevance * 0.4
   155→
   156→
   157→def _signal_relevance(phase: str, signal: SignalFingerprint) -> float:
   158→    """Compute relevance of a signal to a phase.
   159→
   160→    Deterministic mapping from signal features to phase relevance.
   161→    """
   162→    relevance = 0.5  # baseline
   163→
   164→    # Phase-specific relevance boosts
   165→    if phase == "SAFETY" and signal.emotional_valence == "frustrated":
   166→        relevance += 0.3
   167→    elif (phase == "KNOWLEDGE" and signal.domain_signal != "general") or (phase == "EXPERT" and signal.energy_level == "high"):
   168→        relevance += 0.2
   169→    elif phase == "SIGNAL" and signal.urgency == "immediate":
   170→        relevance += 0.25
   171→    elif phase == "DOMAIN" and signal.domain_signal == "vfx":
   172→        relevance += 0.3
   173→    elif phase == "CONSTITUTIONAL" and signal.emotional_valence == "frustrated":
   174→        relevance += 0.2
   175→
   176→    # Cap at 1.0
   177→    return min(relevance, 1.0)
   178→

"""10-phase cascade evaluation for routing decisions.

Fixed evaluation order (PHASES from constants).
Each phase returns a score and routing decision.
Deterministic: same signal fingerprint -> same route, always.
"""

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass

from src.lossless.constants import (
    D_MAP,
    HASH_ALGORITHM,
    PHASES,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SignalFingerprint:
    """A signal to be routed through the cascade.

    Attributes:
        emotional_valence: frustrated / calm / energized
        domain_signal: vfx / web / ai_research / general
        energy_level: high / medium / low / depleted
        urgency: immediate / normal / exploratory
    """

    emotional_valence: str = "calm"
    domain_signal: str = "general"
    energy_level: str = "medium"
    urgency: str = "normal"

    def to_hash(self) -> str:
        """Deterministic hash of the signal fingerprint."""
        parts = [
            f"ev={self.emotional_valence}",
            f"ds={self.domain_signal}",
            f"el={self.energy_level}",
            f"ur={self.urgency}",
        ]
        combined = "|".join(parts)
        h = hashlib.new(HASH_ALGORITHM)
        h.update(combined.encode('utf-8'))
        return h.hexdigest()


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PhaseScore:
    """Score for a single phase in the cascade."""

    phase: str
    score: float
    evaluated: bool  # False if skipped by sparse routing


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CascadeResult:
    """Result of a full cascade evaluation.

    Always contains scores for ALL 10 phases,
    even if sparse routing skipped some.
    """

    phase_scores: tuple  # tuple of PhaseScore, always PHASE_COUNT length
    selected_phases: tuple  # top phases by score
    signal_hash: str
    routing_mode: str  # "dense" or "sparse"

    def get_scores_dict(self) -> dict:
        """Return phase -> score mapping."""
        return {ps.phase: ps.score for ps in self.phase_scores}


def evaluate_cascade(
    signal: SignalFingerprint,
    active_phases: list = None,
    gains: dict = None,
) -> CascadeResult:
    """Evaluate the 10-phase routing cascade.

    Args:
        signal: Signal fingerprint to route.
        active_phases: If provided, only these phases are fully evaluated
                      (sparse routing). All others get default score 0.
        gains: Optional gain modifiers per phase (from injection).

    Returns:
        CascadeResult with scores for all 10 phases.
    """
    if gains is None:
        gains = {}

    signal_hash = signal.to_hash()
    is_sparse = active_phases is not None

    # Evaluate all phases in FIXED canonical order
    phase_scores = []
    for phase in PHASES:
        if is_sparse and phase not in active_phases:
            # Sparse: record as not evaluated
            phase_scores.append(PhaseScore(
                phase=phase, score=0.0, evaluated=False
            ))
        else:
            # Dense: compute score deterministically
            score = _compute_phase_score(phase, signal, signal_hash)

            # Apply gain if present
            g = gains.get(phase, 1.0)
            score = score * g

            phase_scores.append(PhaseScore(
                phase=phase, score=score, evaluated=True
            ))

    # Select top phases by score, using phase priority as tiebreaker
    scored = [(ps.score, PHASES.index(ps.phase), ps.phase)
              for ps in phase_scores if ps.evaluated]
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))  # desc score, asc phase index
    selected = tuple(s[2] for s in scored[:3])

    routing_mode = "sparse" if is_sparse else "dense"

    return CascadeResult(
        phase_scores=tuple(phase_scores),
        selected_phases=selected,
        signal_hash=signal_hash,
        routing_mode=routing_mode,
    )


def _compute_phase_score(
    phase: str, signal: SignalFingerprint, signal_hash: str
) -> float:
    """Compute a deterministic score for a phase given a signal.

    Uses hash-based scoring to ensure determinism.
    """
    # Hash phase + signal for deterministic score
    h = hashlib.new(HASH_ALGORITHM)
    h.update(phase.encode('utf-8'))
    h.update(signal_hash.encode('utf-8'))
    digest = h.hexdigest()

    # Convert first 8 hex chars to a score in [0, 1]
    base_score = int(digest[:8], 16) / (16**8)

    # Weight by receptor density (phases with higher d get higher base scores
    # for relevant signals)
    d = D_MAP.get(phase, 0.5)
    relevance = _signal_relevance(phase, signal)

    return base_score * 0.3 + d * 0.3 + relevance * 0.4


def _signal_relevance(phase: str, signal: SignalFingerprint) -> float:
    """Compute relevance of a signal to a phase.

    Deterministic mapping from signal features to phase relevance.
    """
    relevance = 0.5  # baseline

    # Phase-specific relevance boosts
    if phase == "SAFETY" and signal.emotional_valence == "frustrated":
        relevance += 0.3
    elif (phase == "KNOWLEDGE" and signal.domain_signal != "general") or (phase == "EXPERT" and signal.energy_level == "high"):
        relevance += 0.2
    elif phase == "SIGNAL" and signal.urgency == "immediate":
        relevance += 0.25
    elif phase == "DOMAIN" and signal.domain_signal == "vfx":
        relevance += 0.3
    elif phase == "CONSTITUTIONAL" and signal.emotional_valence == "frustrated":
        relevance += 0.2

    # Cap at 1.0
    return min(relevance, 1.0)

"""Lightning Indexer: sparse routing via 4-feature scoring.

From DeepSeek-V3.2's Sparse Attention: run a cheap 4-feature indexer
to select only the top-3 relevant phases before full evaluation.

DISABLED under classical profile (dissolved routing evaluates all phases).
"""

from src.lossless.routing.cascade import SignalFingerprint

# Fast-path table: signal fingerprint patterns -> top-3 phases
_FAST_PATHS = {
    ("calm", "general", "high", "normal"): ["KNOWLEDGE", "EXPERT", "DOMAIN"],
    ("calm", "general", "medium", "normal"): ["KNOWLEDGE", "EXPERT", "DOMAIN"],
    ("frustrated", "general", "medium", "immediate"): [
        "CONSTITUTIONAL", "SAFETY", "SIGNAL",
    ],
    ("energized", "general", "high", "exploratory"): [
        "KNOWLEDGE", "SIGNAL", "EXPERT",
    ],
    ("calm", "general", "depleted", "normal"): [
        "SAFETY", "SIGNAL", "EXPERT",
    ],
}

# Calibration: use dense for first N exchanges
_CALIBRATION_EXCHANGES = 10


class LightningIndexer:
    """Sparse routing indexer that selects top-3 phases.

    Dense fallback for:
    - First 10 exchanges (calibration)
    - Dissolved routing mode
    - Novel signal fingerprints (not in fast-path table)
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._exchange_count = 0
        self._session_fast_paths = {}  # novel patterns promoted mid-session

    def select_phases(
        self,
        signal: SignalFingerprint,
        routing_mode: str = "standard",
    ) -> list:
        """Select which phases to evaluate.

        Args:
            signal: Signal fingerprint.
            routing_mode: "standard", "dissolved", or "integrative".

        Returns:
            List of phase names to evaluate, or None for dense (all phases).
        """
        self._exchange_count += 1

        # Dissolved mode: always dense
        if routing_mode == "dissolved":
            return None

        # Calibration period: always dense
        if self._exchange_count <= _CALIBRATION_EXCHANGES:
            return None

        # Check fast-path table
        fp_key = (
            signal.emotional_valence,
            signal.domain_signal,
            signal.energy_level,
            signal.urgency,
        )

        if fp_key in _FAST_PATHS:
            return list(_FAST_PATHS[fp_key])

        # Check session-local fast paths
        if fp_key in self._session_fast_paths:
            return list(self._session_fast_paths[fp_key])

        # Novel fingerprint: use dense, record for potential promotion
        self._record_novel(fp_key)
        return None

    def _record_novel(self, fp_key: tuple) -> None:
        """Record a novel fingerprint for potential fast-path promotion.

        If seen 3+ times, promote to session-local fast path.
        """
        if not hasattr(self, '_novel_counts'):
            self._novel_counts = {}

        self._novel_counts[fp_key] = self._novel_counts.get(fp_key, 0) + 1

        if self._novel_counts[fp_key] >= 3:
            # Promote to session-local fast path with default phases
            self._session_fast_paths[fp_key] = [
                "KNOWLEDGE", "EXPERT", "SIGNAL",
            ]

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Reset indexer state for a new session."""
        self._exchange_count = 0
        self._session_fast_paths = {}
        self._novel_counts = {}

"""Dual-path routing: clean + dissolved parallel routes.

At baseline and microdose, only the clean path runs.
At classical/dissolved, both paths run and provenance is tracked.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from src.lossless.constants import PHASES, PROFILES
from src.lossless.injection.state import InjectionState
from src.lossless.routing.cascade import (
    CascadeResult,
    SignalFingerprint,
    evaluate_cascade,
)
from src.lossless.routing.indexer import LightningIndexer
from src.lossless.routing.provenance import ProvenanceRecord, ProvenanceTracker


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DualPathResult:
    """Result of dual-path routing evaluation.

    Always contains clean_route. dissolved_route is None
    when routing mode is not "dissolved".
    """

    clean_route: CascadeResult
    dissolved_route: CascadeResult  # None if not dissolved
    blend_alpha: float
    routing_mode: str
    provenance: tuple  # tuple of ProvenanceRecord


def evaluate_dual_path(
    signal: SignalFingerprint,
    injection_state: InjectionState,
    indexer: LightningIndexer = None,
    provenance_tracker: ProvenanceTracker = None,
) -> DualPathResult:
    """Evaluate dual-path routing.

    Clean path always runs (standard thresholds).
    Dissolved path runs in addition when routing mode is "dissolved".

    Args:
        signal: Signal fingerprint.
        injection_state: Current injection state.
        indexer: Optional Lightning Indexer for sparse routing.
        provenance_tracker: Optional provenance recorder.

    Returns:
        DualPathResult with both routes.
    """
    if provenance_tracker is None:
        provenance_tracker = ProvenanceTracker()

    routing_mode = PROFILES[injection_state.profile]["routing"]
    alpha = injection_state.alpha

    # Determine sparse routing phases
    active_phases = None
    if indexer is not None:
        active_phases = indexer.select_phases(signal, routing_mode)

    # Clean route: always evaluate with standard gains (all 1.0)
    clean_route = evaluate_cascade(signal, active_phases=active_phases)

    # Dissolved route: evaluate with injection gains
    dissolved_route = clean_route  # default: same as clean
    if routing_mode == "dissolved":
        # Dissolved routing evaluates ALL phases (no sparse)
        gains = {}
        for phase in PHASES:
            gains[phase] = injection_state.get_gain(phase)

        dissolved_route = evaluate_cascade(
            signal, active_phases=None, gains=gains
        )

    # Record provenance
    dominant = "clean"
    if routing_mode == "dissolved" and alpha > 0.5:
        dominant = "dissolved"

    record = ProvenanceRecord(
        signal_hash=signal.to_hash(),
        clean_selected=clean_route.selected_phases,
        dissolved_selected=dissolved_route.selected_phases,
        blend_alpha=alpha,
        dominant_path=dominant,
        routing_mode=routing_mode,
    )
    provenance_tracker.record(record)

    return DualPathResult(
        clean_route=clean_route,
        dissolved_route=dissolved_route,
        blend_alpha=alpha,
        routing_mode=routing_mode,
        provenance=tuple(provenance_tracker.get_records()),
    )

1→"""Expert selection from routing decisions.
     2→
     3→Selects the best expert based on routing cascade scores,
     4→using fixed priority order as tiebreaker.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→import hashlib
     8→
     9→from src.lossless.constants import EXPERTS, HASH_ALGORITHM
    10→from src.lossless.experts.registry import ExpertSpec, get_expert_registry
    11→from src.lossless.routing.cascade import CascadeResult
    12→
    13→
    14→def select_expert(
    15→    cascade_result: CascadeResult,
    16→    expert_weights: dict = None,
    17→) -> ExpertSpec:
    18→    """Select the best expert based on routing scores.
    19→
    20→    Uses hash-based deterministic scoring with fixed priority tiebreaking.
    21→
    22→    Args:
    23→        cascade_result: Result from cascade evaluation.
    24→        expert_weights: Optional per-expert weight adjustments.
    25→
    26→    Returns:
    27→        Selected Expert.
    28→    """
    29→    registry = get_expert_registry()
    30→
    31→    if expert_weights is None:
    32→        expert_weights = {}
    33→
    34→    # Score each expert deterministically
    35→    scored = []
    36→    signal_hash = cascade_result.signal_hash
    37→
    38→    for i, name in enumerate(EXPERTS):
    39→        # Hash-based score: deterministic from signal + expert name
    40→        h = hashlib.new(HASH_ALGORITHM)
    41→        h.update(signal_hash.encode('utf-8'))
    42→        h.update(name.encode('utf-8'))
    43→        digest = h.hexdigest()
    44→        base_score = int(digest[:8], 16) / (16**8)
    45→
    46→        # Apply phase relevance from cascade
    47→        phase_boost = _phase_relevance_for_expert(
    48→            name, cascade_result.get_scores_dict()
    49→        )
    50→
    51→        # Apply external weight if provided
    52→        weight = expert_weights.get(name, 1.0)
    53→
    54→        total_score = (base_score * 0.3 + phase_boost * 0.7) * weight
    55→
    56→        # Priority as tiebreaker (lower priority index = better)
    57→        scored.append((total_score, i, name))
    58→
    59→    # Sort: descending score, ascending priority index
    60→    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))
    61→
    62→    selected_name = scored[0][2]
    63→    return registry[selected_name]
    64→
    65→
    66→def _phase_relevance_for_expert(
    67→    expert_name: str, phase_scores: dict
    68→) -> float:
    69→    """Compute how relevant the phase scores are to an expert.
    70→
    71→    Deterministic mapping from expert to phase affinities.
    72→    """
    73→    # Expert-phase affinity matrix (deterministic)

"""Expert selection from routing decisions.

Selects the best expert based on routing cascade scores,
using fixed priority order as tiebreaker.
"""

import hashlib

from src.lossless.constants import EXPERTS, HASH_ALGORITHM
from src.lossless.experts.registry import ExpertSpec, get_expert_registry
from src.lossless.routing.cascade import CascadeResult


def select_expert(
    cascade_result: CascadeResult,
    expert_weights: dict = None,
) -> ExpertSpec:
    """Select the best expert based on routing scores.

    Uses hash-based deterministic scoring with fixed priority tiebreaking.

    Args:
        cascade_result: Result from cascade evaluation.
        expert_weights: Optional per-expert weight adjustments.

    Returns:
        Selected Expert.
    """
    registry = get_expert_registry()

    if expert_weights is None:
        expert_weights = {}

    # Score each expert deterministically
    scored = []
    signal_hash = cascade_result.signal_hash

    for i, name in enumerate(EXPERTS):
        # Hash-based score: deterministic from signal + expert name
        h = hashlib.new(HASH_ALGORITHM)
        h.update(signal_hash.encode('utf-8'))
        h.update(name.encode('utf-8'))
        digest = h.hexdigest()
        base_score = int(digest[:8], 16) / (16**8)

        # Apply phase relevance from cascade
        phase_boost = _phase_relevance_for_expert(
            name, cascade_result.get_scores_dict()
        )

        # Apply external weight if provided
        weight = expert_weights.get(name, 1.0)

        total_score = (base_score * 0.3 + phase_boost * 0.7) * weight

        # Priority as tiebreaker (lower priority index = better)
        scored.append((total_score, i, name))

    # Sort: descending score, ascending priority index
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))

    selected_name = scored[0][2]
    return registry[selected_name]


def _phase_relevance_for_expert(
    expert_name: str, phase_scores: dict
) -> float:
    """Compute how relevant the phase scores are to an expert.

    Deterministic mapping from expert to phase affinities.
    """
    # Expert-phase affinity matrix (deterministic)
    affinities = {
        "Validator": {"SAFETY": 0.4, "CONSTITUTIONAL": 0.3, "SIGNAL": 0.3},
        "Scaffolder": {"KNOWLEDGE": 0.4, "EXPERT": 0.3, "PROJECT": 0.3},
        "Restorer": {"SAFETY": 0.3, "SIGNAL": 0.4, "CONSENT": 0.3},
        "Refocuser": {"SIGNAL": 0.4, "PROJECT": 0.3, "DOMAIN": 0.3},
        "Celebrator": {"SIGNAL": 0.3, "EXPERT": 0.4, "DOMAIN": 0.3},
        "Socratic": {"KNOWLEDGE": 0.5, "DOMAIN": 0.3, "EXPERT": 0.2},
        "Direct": {"EXPERT": 0.4, "DOMAIN": 0.3, "KNOWLEDGE": 0.3},
    }

    if expert_name not in affinities:
        return 0.5

    expert_affinities = affinities[expert_name]
    # Kahan summation for numerical stability
    total = 0.0
    comp = 0.0
    for phase, weight in sorted(expert_affinities.items()):
        score = phase_scores.get(phase, 0.0)
        y = score * weight - comp
        t = total + y
        comp = (t - total) - y
        total = t

    return total

"""Expert definitions and priority registry.

Expert priority is FIXED:
Validator > Scaffolder > Restorer > Refocuser > Celebrator > Socratic > Direct

This order NEVER changes under injection. What changes is how MUCH
each expert contributes (bleeding coefficient).
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from src.lossless.constants import EXPERTS


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ExpertSpec:
    """Definition of a single expert in the MoE system."""

    name: str
    priority: int  # lower = higher priority
    description: str

    @property
    def is_primary(self) -> bool:
        return self.priority <= 2


_EXPERT_DESCRIPTIONS = {
    "Validator": "Validates emotional state and redirects negative spirals",
    "Scaffolder": "Breaks down complex tasks into manageable steps",
    "Restorer": "Helps user recover from burnout or depletion",
    "Refocuser": "Redirects wandering attention to current goals",
    "Celebrator": "Acknowledges progress and maintains motivation",
    "Socratic": "Guides exploration through questioning",
    "Direct": "Provides direct expert assistance with minimal intervention",
}


def get_expert_registry() -> dict:
    """Build the expert registry with fixed priority ordering.

    Returns:
        Dict mapping expert name to Expert object.
        Iteration order follows EXPERTS list from constants.
    """
    registry = {}
    for i, name in enumerate(EXPERTS):
        registry[name] = ExpertSpec(
            name=name,
            priority=i,
            description=_EXPERT_DESCRIPTIONS.get(name, ""),
        )
    return registry


def get_experts_by_priority() -> list:
    """Return experts sorted by priority (highest priority first)."""
    registry = get_expert_registry()
    return [registry[name] for name in EXPERTS]


def get_expert_names() -> list:
    """Return expert names in priority order."""
    return list(EXPERTS)

"""Cross-expert information bleeding.

Tracked via the MixingTracker from Agent 3.
Bleeding only occurs between modulated phases.
Anchor phases are NEVER involved in bleeding.
"""

from src.lossless.constants import ANCHOR_PHASES, MODULATED_PHASES, PROFILES
from src.lossless.injection.state import InjectionState


def apply_bleeding(
    expert_contributions: dict,
    injection_state: InjectionState,
) -> dict:
    """Apply cross-expert bleeding to expert contributions.

    Args:
        expert_contributions: Phase-name -> contribution score mapping.
        injection_state: Current injection state (has mixing_tracker).

    Returns:
        New dict with bleeding applied to modulated phases only.
        Anchor phase contributions are UNCHANGED.
    """
    result = {}

    # Copy anchor phases unchanged
    for phase in sorted(expert_contributions.keys()):
        if phase in ANCHOR_PHASES:
            result[phase] = expert_contributions[phase]

    # Get modulated phase contributions as a vector
    mod_phases = sorted(MODULATED_PHASES)
    signal = []
    for phase in mod_phases:
        signal.append(expert_contributions.get(phase, 0.0))

    # Apply mixing if there's cross-expert bleeding
    mixed = injection_state.mixing_tracker.mix(signal)

    # Write back
    for i, phase in enumerate(mod_phases):
        result[phase] = mixed[i]

    return result


def get_bleeding_coefficient(profile_name: str) -> float:
    """Get the cross-expert bleeding coefficient for a profile.

    Args:
        profile_name: Profile name.

    Returns:
        Bleeding coefficient in [0.0, 1.0).
    """
    if profile_name not in PROFILES:
        return 0.0
    return PROFILES[profile_name]["cross_expert"]

"""Expert execution orchestrator.

Coordinates expert selection, bleeding, and execution
with full provenance tracking.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from src.lossless.constants import PHASES, PROFILES
from src.lossless.experts.bleeding import apply_bleeding
from src.lossless.experts.registry import ExpertSpec
from src.lossless.experts.selector import select_expert
from src.lossless.injection.state import InjectionState
from src.lossless.routing.cascade import CascadeResult


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ExpertResult:
    """Result of expert execution.

    Attributes:
        selected_expert: The expert that was selected.
        expert_scores: All expert contribution scores.
        bleeding_applied: Whether cross-expert bleeding was applied.
        profile_name: Injection profile active during execution.
    """

    selected_expert: ExpertSpec
    expert_scores: tuple  # tuple of (phase, score) pairs
    bleeding_applied: bool
    profile_name: str


def execute_expert(
    cascade_result: CascadeResult,
    injection_state: InjectionState,
) -> ExpertResult:
    """Execute expert selection and contribution calculation.

    Args:
        cascade_result: Routing cascade result.
        injection_state: Current injection state.

    Returns:
        ExpertResult with selected expert and scores.
    """
    profile_name = injection_state.profile
    cross_expert = PROFILES[profile_name]["cross_expert"]

    # Select primary expert
    expert = select_expert(cascade_result)

    # Compute expert contributions per phase
    contributions = {}
    phase_scores = cascade_result.get_scores_dict()
    for phase in PHASES:
        contributions[phase] = phase_scores.get(phase, 0.0)

    # Apply bleeding if cross-expert coefficient is non-zero
    bleeding_applied = False
    if cross_expert > 0.0 and injection_state.active:
        contributions = apply_bleeding(contributions, injection_state)
        bleeding_applied = True

    return ExpertResult(
        selected_expert=expert,
        expert_scores=tuple(sorted(contributions.items())),
        bleeding_applied=bleeding_applied,
        profile_name=profile_name,
    )

1→"""USDA file parser for the Lossless Signal Architecture.
     2→
     3→Reads .usda files, extracts prims with attributes.
     4→Returns CognitivePrim objects from the schema module.
     5→
     6→CRITICAL: This parser is DETERMINISTIC.
     7→Same file content -> same parse tree, always.
     8→No dict iteration without sorted keys.
     9→No set iteration without sorted().
    10→"""
    11→
    12→import re
    13→from pathlib import Path
    14→
    15→from src.lossless.schema.prims import CognitivePrim
    16→
    17→# Regex patterns for USDA parsing
    18→_DEF_RE = re.compile(r'\bdef\s+"([^"]+)"\s*(?:\((.*?)\)\s*)?\{', re.DOTALL)
    19→_OVER_RE = re.compile(r'\bover\s+"([^"]+)"\s*\{', re.DOTALL)
    20→_SUBLAYERS_RE = re.compile(r'subLayers\s*=\s*\[(.*?)\]', re.DOTALL)
    21→_SUBLAYER_PATH_RE = re.compile(r'@([^@]+)@')
    22→_TRIPLE_STR_RE = re.compile(
    23→    r'(?:string|custom\s+string)\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*"""(.*?)"""', re.DOTALL
    24→)
    25→_SINGLE_STR_RE = re.compile(
    26→    r'(?:string|custom\s+string)\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"'
    27→)
    28→_INT_RE = re.compile(r'(?:int|custom\s+int)\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*(-?\d+)')
    29→_BOOL_RE = re.compile(r'(?:bool|custom\s+bool)\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*(true|false)')
    30→_FLOAT_RE = re.compile(
    31→    r'(?:float|custom\s+float)\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*(-?[\d.]+(?:e[+-]?\d+)?)'
    32→)
    33→_STR_ARRAY_RE = re.compile(
    34→    r'(?:string\[\]|custom\s+string\[\])\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*\[(.*?)\]', re.DOTALL
    35→)
    36→_DOC_RE = re.compile(r'doc\s*=\s*(?:"""(.*?)"""|"([^"]*)")', re.DOTALL)
    37→
    38→
    39→def parse_sublayers(text: str, root_dir: Path) -> list:
    40→    """Extract sublayer paths from a root composition file.
    41→
    42→    Returns paths in declaration order (strongest first).
    43→    Skips commented-out lines.
    44→    """
    45→    m = _SUBLAYERS_RE.search(text)
    46→    if not m:
    47→        return []
    48→
    49→    block = m.group(1)
    50→    paths = []
    51→    for line in block.splitlines():
    52→        stripped = line.strip()
    53→        if stripped.startswith('#'):
    54→            continue
    55→        pm = _SUBLAYER_PATH_RE.search(stripped)
    56→        if pm:
    57→            rel = pm.group(1)
    58→            abs_path = (root_dir / rel).resolve()
    59→            paths.append(abs_path)
    60→    return paths
    61→
    62→
    63→def parse_file(path: Path) -> tuple:
    64→    """Parse a USDA file into (defs, overs).
    65→
    66→    Returns:
    67→        (list[CognitivePrim], list[CognitivePrim]) where first list
    68→        is def prims and second is over prims.
    69→    """
    70→    text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    71→    filename = path.name
    72→    defs = []
    73→    overs = []
    74→
    75→    pos = 0
    76→    while pos < len(text):
    77→        def_m = _DEF_RE.search(text, pos)
    78→        over_m = _OVER_RE.search(text, pos)
    79→
    80→        candidates = []
    81→        if def_m:
    82→            candidates.append(('def', def_m))
    83→        if over_m:
    84→            candidates.append(('over', over_m))
    85→
    86→        if not candidates:
    87→            break
    88→
    89→        candidates.sort(key=lambda c: c[1].start())
    90→        kind, match = candidates[0]
    91→
    92→        brace_pos = match.end() - 1
    93→        body_end = _find_matching_brace(text, brace_pos)
    94→        if body_end == -1:
    95→            pos = match.end()
    96→            continue
    97→
    98→        body = text[brace_pos + 1:body_end]
    99→        name = match.group(1)
   100→
   101→        if kind == 'def':
   102→            if name == "Preamble":
   103→                pos = body_end + 1
   104→                continue
   105→            metadata = match.group(2) or ""
   106→            prim = _parse_def_prim(name, metadata, body, filename)
   107→            defs.append(prim)
   108→        else:
   109→            prim = _parse_over_prim(name, body, filename)
   110→            overs.append(prim)
   111→
   112→        pos = body_end + 1
   113→
   114→    return defs, overs
   115→
   116→
   117→def _parse_def_prim(
   118→    name: str, metadata: str, body: str, filename: str
   119→) -> CognitivePrim:
   120→    """Parse a def prim into a CognitivePrim."""
   121→    doc = ""
   122→    doc_m = _DOC_RE.search(metadata)
   123→    if doc_m:
   124→        doc = doc_m.group(1) or doc_m.group(2) or ""
   125→
   126→    clean_body = _strip_nested(body)
   127→    attrs = _parse_attrs(clean_body)
   128→
   129→    return CognitivePrim(
   130→        name=name,
   131→        phase=attrs.get("phase_classification", "DEFAULT"),
   132→        prim_type="def",
   133→        markdown_content=attrs.get("markdown_content", ""),
   134→        priority=attrs.get("priority", 50),
   135→        enabled=attrs.get("enabled", True),
   136→        source_file=filename,
   137→        doc=doc,
   138→        attributes=tuple(sorted(attrs.items())),
   139→    )
   140→
   141→
   142→def _parse_over_prim(
   143→    name: str, body: str, filename: str
   144→) -> CognitivePrim:
   145→    """Parse an over prim into a CognitivePrim."""
   146→    attrs = _parse_attrs(body)
   147→
   148→    return CognitivePrim(
   149→        name=name,
   150→        phase=attrs.get("phase_classification", "DEFAULT"),
   151→        prim_type="over",
   152→        markdown_content=attrs.get("markdown_content", ""),
   153→        priority=attrs.get("priority", 50),
   154→        enabled=attrs.get("enabled", True),
   155→        source_file=filename,
   156→        doc="",
   157→        attributes=tuple(sorted(attrs.items())),
   158→    )
   159→
   160→
   161→def _parse_attrs(body: str) -> dict:
   162→    """Extract typed attributes from a prim body."""
   163→    attrs = {}
   164→
   165→    for m in _TRIPLE_STR_RE.finditer(body):
   166→        attrs[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
   167→
   168→    for m in _SINGLE_STR_RE.finditer(body):
   169→        if m.group(1) not in attrs:
   170→            attrs[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
